summary: William Price (1780–1830) was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary and served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College (~1813–1830).

William R. Hutchison (1930–2005) was a scholar of religious studies and history. He earned degrees from Oxford (~1951–1953) and Yale (~1953–1956), later holding posts at Yale, Hunter College, Wisconsin-Madison, American University (~1960–1968), and Harvard (1968).

William R. LaFleur (1936–2010) worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago, and taught at Princeton (~1971–1976), UCLA (~1978–1989), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–2010).

William Rainey Harper (1856–1906) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and served as professor at Yale (1886) and president of the University of Chicago (1891–1906) and Bradley University (~1897–1899).

William Roxburgh (1751–1815) worked in Indology, studying at Edinburgh under John Hope and Alexander Monro, and at Aberdeen. His posts included Madras Medical Service, Samalkot Experimental Farm, and head of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1793).

William S. Waldron works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (–1990) under Minoru Kiyota, Ichijo Ogawa, and Seiki Miyashita, and held posts at Otani University and Middlebury College (attested 2003).

William Stede (1882–1958) was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He served as an editor for the Pali Text Society (~1916–1925) and held a post at SOAS University of London (~1925–1949).

William Van Gordon is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University (attested 2015).

William Ward (1769–1823) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Ewood Hall Academy under John Fawcett (1797), served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission (~1799–1823), and founded Serampore College (1818).

William Wilson Hunter (1840–1900) worked in history and Indology. Educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887) and was vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1886).

William Woodville Rockhill (1854–1914) was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Lycée Condorcet and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr, and studied under Léon Feer and Philippe Édouard Foucaux (~1877–1883).

William Wright (1830–1889) was a linguist who studied at St Andrews, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leiden. He held posts at University College London, Trinity College Dublin, the British Museum (1861–1870), and Cambridge as Adams Professor of Arabic (1870–1889).

Willibald Kirfel (1885–1964) was an Indologist. He earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, working there as a librarian and privatdozent (1920) before becoming full professor (1922).

Wilt L. Idema (born 1944) is a Sinologist. He earned degrees from Leiden University, where he studied under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé, and served as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden (1976–1999) and Harvard University (2000–2013).

Winfred P. Lehmann (1916–2007) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1937–1941) and served as a professor at the University of Texas at Austin (~1949–1986).

Winfred Robert Martin (died 1915) worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and later as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Wing-tsit Chan (1901–1994) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard University (~1924–1929) and held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1936–1942), Dartmouth College (~1942–1966), and Chatham University (~1966–1982).

Winnifred Fallers Sullivan (born 1950) works in religious studies. She studied at Cornell and the University of Chicago, later holding posts at Washington and Lee, the University of Chicago, University at Buffalo, and Indiana University Bloomington (~2010).
Winston Kyan is a scholar in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Hung Wu and Linda Seidel.

Wm. Theodore de Bary (1919–2017) was a Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology scholar. Educated at Columbia, Harvard, and the U.S. Navy Japanese Language School, he served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia (1953–2017).
